messages:
Laura (arch): Quick follow-up on the 'staged proxy' idea from the RFC — propose extracting the initial request proxy/handshake out of the runtime into a tiny, language-agnostic shim. Goals: decouple KV-cache ownership, make private deployments lighter, and allow different transports (unix socket vs HTTP). Concerns: perf/regression risk, tracing, canarying, and deployed surface area. Thoughts?

Mike (eng-runtime): I like decoupling. Sidecar gives isolation but adds IPC cost. Shared lib is fastest but couples releases. We should measure p95/p99 token latency impact with a microbenchmark.

Priya (eng-platform): Also think about model routing policy; proxy needs to forward model selection decisions or expose a contract. If proxy is thin, it should only forward metadata and never own routing state.

Sam (eng-sre): Observability note — ensure correlation-id flows end-to-end. Also need a fallback path if the proxy crashes. Circuit-breaker + health-checks in front.

Mike (eng-runtime): For KV cache ownership: alternative is runtime retains ownership but exposes a socket API for cache fetches. Proxy authors shouldn't modify cache schema. We'll define a minimal RPC: GET_PREFIX(prefix_hash) -> {kv_blob | MISS}.

Laura (arch): Strawman handshake (pseudo):
```text
client -> proxy: {request_id, model_hint, prefix_hash}
proxy -> runtime: unix-socket call: {request_id, prefix_hash}
runtime -> proxy: {kv_blob | MISS}
proxy -> model: attach kv_blob and forward
```
If MISS, runtime can return MISS and proxy proceeds; runtime can async prefill.

Priya (eng-platform): +1. Also need contract versioning header, e.g. X-Proxy-API: v1. On-prem customers may upgrade proxies independently — compatibility matters.

Sam (eng-sre): Canary plan: deploy proxy to one Dedicated pool, route ~5% traffic, monitor p99 latency, cache hit ratio, and error rates for 48h.

Mike (eng-runtime): I'll do a 3-day microbench spike (latency delta, CPU). Priya can prototype the unix-socket client in Go. Laura can update RFC with a contract draft.

Laura (arch): Decision: proceed with 'thin-proxy' approach (unix-socket RPC, contracted headers, runtime retains cache ownership). Action items: Mike -> spike, Priya -> prototype, Sam -> canary pipeline, Laura -> RFC update. Timeline: Spike by 2024-05-01, Prototype by 2024-05-10, Canary week of 2024-05-13. Any blockers?

Priya (eng-platform): Note: need a security review for socket permissions and KMS access in Private. I'll schedule that.

ops-bot: CI job created: arch/proxy-spike #42 — logs at https://ci.internal/arch/proxy-spike/42 :rocket:

Sam (eng-sre): Also add a quick rollback flag: RUNTIME_PROXY_ENABLED = true/false for immediate rollback.

Laura (arch): Thanks all. I'll post the RFC update draft in #architecture tomorrow. :handshake:
